editorial:
You know that feeling when a first date goes perfectly, then everything falls apart? That is the spark behind this romantic comedy. Bea and Ben share one amazing night, but a misunderstanding turns their chemistry into cold silence. When they end up at a destination wedding in Australia, they decide to fake a relationship to keep family drama low and maybe make their exes jealous. The movie leans into sunny locations, awkward moments, and sharp banter, giving you a fun escape that feels light without being boring.

Sydney Sweeney and Glen Powell carry the movie with easy charm, and their back-and-forth keeps scenes moving even when the plot gets predictable. The supporting cast adds laughs, while the wedding setting gives everything a bright, vacation feel. It is not deep, and some jokes land better than others, but the pacing stays quick and the romance has enough heat to keep you invested.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Bea and Ben stop pretending and admit they actually love each other. After a big misunderstanding at the wedding, Ben chases Bea down and they finally talk honestly instead of hiding behind jokes. The movie ends with them choosing to be together, turning their fake couple act into a real relationship. It is a sweet, simple finish that rewards the slow burn and gives you the happy ending you expected.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves breezy rom-coms and destination wedding chaos.
